title: C++ References
description: References in C++: binding rules, references as aliases, pass by reference, const references, returning references, the difference from pointers, auto& in range-for and dangling references.

descriptionI18n.zh-Hant: C++ 參考：綁定規則、以別名方式作用、傳參考、const 參考、回傳參考、與指標的差異、範圍 for 中的 auto&，以及懸空參考。

questions.prompt: After `int x = 1; int& r = x; r = 7;`, what is the value of `x`?

prompt.zh-Hant: 執行 `int x = 1; int& r = x; r = 7;` 之後，`x` 的值是甚麼？

explanation.zh-Hant: `r` 只是 `x` 的別名，對 `r` 賦值就是對 `x` 賦值，所以 `x` 變成 7。

options.text: Unspecified
The address of `r`

questions.explanation: `r` is just another name for `x`, so assigning to `r` assigns to `x`; the value becomes 7.

questions.prompt: Which statement about declaring a reference is correct?

prompt.zh-Hant: 關於參考的宣告，下列哪一個敘述正確？

a.zh-Hant: 可以先宣告，之後再綁定到物件

b.zh-Hant: 必須在宣告的同時初始化

c.zh-Hant: 綁定後可以改綁到另一個物件

d.zh-Hant: 未初始化時預設為空參考

explanation.zh-Hant: 參考一定要在宣告時綁定到一個既存物件，而且終生不能再改綁；C++ 沒有「空參考」。

options.text: It can be declared first and bound to an object later
It must be initialised in its declaration
It can be rebound to another object later
If uninitialised it defaults to a null reference

questions.explanation: A reference must be bound to an existing object when it is declared and can never be rebound; C++ has no null reference.

questions.prompt: What does declaring a function parameter as `int&` achieve?

prompt.zh-Hant: 把函式參數宣告為 `int&` 有甚麼效果？

a.zh-Hant: 函式內操作的是呼叫端傳入的物件，修改會反映回去

b.zh-Hant: 引數一定會被複製一份到函式內

explanation.zh-Hant: `int&` 讓參數成為引數的別名，函式內的修改直接作用在呼叫端的物件上，不會產生複本。

options.text: The function works on the caller's own object, so changes are visible to the caller
The argument is always copied into the function
The caller may only pass a literal constant
The argument must be a pointer

questions.explanation: An `int&` parameter is an alias for the caller's argument, so modifications act on the original object and no copy is made.

questions.prompt: Which function safely returns a reference?

prompt.zh-Hant: 下列哪一個函式可以安全地回傳參考？

b.zh-Hant: 回傳靜態物件或成員的參考，該物件活得比呼叫更久

c.zh-Hant: 回傳函式內建立的暫時物件參考

d.zh-Hant: 回傳已 delete 的堆積物件參考

explanation.zh-Hant: 回傳的參考必須指向呼叫結束後仍存在的物件；區域變數與暫時物件在函式結束時就銷毀，會形成懸空參考。

options.text: Return a reference to a local variable
Return a reference to a static object or a member that outlives the call
Return a reference to a temporary created inside the function
Return a reference to heap memory that was already deleted

questions.explanation: A returned reference must designate an object that still exists after the call returns. Locals and temporaries die with the function, leaving a dangling reference.

questions.prompt: Which statements about `const` references are true? Select all that apply.

prompt.zh-Hant: 關於 `const` 參考，下列哪些敘述正確？可多選。

a.zh-Hant: `const int&` 可以綁定到暫時物件

b.zh-Hant: 不能透過該參考修改被參考的物件

c.zh-Hant: 被參考的物件從此對所有人都是唯讀

d.zh-Hant: 常用來傳遞大型物件而避免複製

explanation.zh-Hant: const 參考可綁定暫時物件、延長其壽命，且只限制「透過這個參考」的修改；其他人仍可經由非 const 途徑修改原物件。

options.text: `const int&` can bind to a temporary
The referred-to object cannot be modified through that reference
The referred-to object becomes read-only for everyone
It is commonly used to pass large objects without copying

questions.explanation: A `const` reference can bind to a temporary (extending its lifetime) and only restricts modification through that reference; other non-const paths can still change the object. It is the standard way to pass large objects cheaply.

questions.prompt: Which statements about references versus pointers are true? Select all that apply.

prompt.zh-Hant: 關於參考與指標的比較，下列哪些敘述正確？可多選。

a.zh-Hant: 合法的參考一定指向某個物件，不會是空值

b.zh-Hant: 指標可以改指向別的物件，參考不行

c.zh-Hant: 對參考套用 `&` 會得到被參考物件的位址

d.zh-Hant: `sizeof(r)` 得到的是參考本身的位元組數

explanation.zh-Hant: 參考是物件的別名，沒有獨立身分：`&r` 就是原物件位址，`sizeof(r)` 是原物件大小；改綁與空值都只屬於指標。

options.text: A valid reference always designates an object and is never null
A pointer can be reseated to another object; a reference cannot
Applying `&` to a reference yields the address of the referred-to object
`sizeof(r)` yields the size of the reference itself

questions.explanation: A reference is an alias with no separate identity: `&r` is the referent's address and `sizeof(r)` is the referent's size. Only pointers can be null or reseated.

questions.prompt: A reference can be reseated to refer to a different object after it has been bound.

prompt.zh-Hant: 參考綁定之後，可以改綁到另一個物件。

explanation.zh-Hant: `int& r = a; r = b;` 是把 b 的值指派給 a，不是改綁；參考一旦綁定就固定指向同一物件。

questions.explanation: `int& r = a; r = b;` assigns b's value to a; it does not rebind. Once bound, a reference always designates the same object.

questions.prompt: Using `auto&` in a range-for loop allows the loop body to modify the container's elements in place.

prompt.zh-Hant: 在範圍 for 迴圈中使用 `auto&`，可以讓迴圈本體直接修改容器的元素。

explanation.zh-Hant: `for (auto& x : v)` 讓 x 成為每個元素的參考，因此 `x *= 2` 會改到容器本身；用 `auto` 只會拿到複本。

questions.explanation: `for (auto& x : v)` binds `x` to each element, so `x *= 2` changes the container itself. Plain `auto` copies each element and leaves the container untouched.

questions.prompt: A parameter declared as `const std::string&` avoids a ____ of the argument when the function is called.

prompt.zh-Hant: 參數宣告為 `const std::string&` 可以避免呼叫函式時對引數進行一次 ____。

explanation.zh-Hant: 傳值會複製整個字串；const 參考只傳別名，既省成本又保證函式內不改動原物件。

questions.explanation: Passing by value copies the whole string; a `const` reference passes only an alias, avoiding the copy while promising not to modify the original.

questions.prompt: What is a dangling reference? Give one example of how it is created.

prompt.zh-Hant: 甚麼是懸空參考（dangling reference）？舉出一個產生它的例子。

model.zh-Hant: 懸空參考是指參考仍然存在，但所綁定的物件已經結束存活期，此時透過它存取就是未定義行為。例如函式回傳區域變數的參考：`int& f() { int x = 1; return x; }`，呼叫端拿到 `f()` 後 x 已銷毀；或是保留了區域容器元素的參考，容器之後被解構。

explanation.zh-Hant: 重點是「參考不比它所綁定的物件活得更久」；回傳區域變數參考、綁定已 delete 的物件都是典型例子。

answer.model: A dangling reference is a reference whose referent has already been destroyed; using it afterwards is undefined behaviour. A typical example is returning a reference to a local: `int& f() { int x = 1; return x; }` — `x` dies when `f` returns, so the caller's reference dangles. Keeping a reference to an element of a container that is later destroyed has the same effect.

questions.explanation: The rule is that a reference must never outlive its referent; returning a local reference and binding to deleted storage are the classic cases.
